source.title_on_document: How and for Whom Using Generative AI Affects Creativity: A Field Experiment

supplement.holds: The main text describes item-level cognitive-job-resource analyses in Supplemental Tables S1–S4 and moderation/practical-significance robustness tests in Supplemental Sections S6–S8 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6). For models without controls, the Results cite Supplemental Table S5 Model 4, whereas footnote 2 cites Supplemental Materials S4 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5). The usefulness coefficient without controls is also printed in the main text. The supplement is absent from the supplied PDF and was not retrieved; its contents and internal locators were not independently checked.

paper_design_summary: In a Chinese technology consulting firm, nonmanagerial employees were individually randomized to personal ChatGPT accounts with usage examples or no LLM assistance; 250 employees were analyzed (PDF pp. 5-6, Participants and Procedure; PDF p. 10, Table 3). At the end of approximately one week, supervisors rated general creative performance and external raters scored the novelty and usefulness of employees' written privacy-protection suggestions. The supervisor scale does not score a specified output; the written-response measures do, but the document does not specify AI availability while those responses were composed or the external raters' qualifications (PDF p. 6, Method).

arms.name: LLM assistance
arms.description: Personal ChatGPT accounts with usage examples; accounts were not to be shared or discussed with others. All treated employees reported use and logs confirmed use; logged frequency M = 33.72, SD = 8.17 (PDF p. 6, Participants and Procedure; Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

arms.name: Control (no LLM assistance)
arms.description: No LLM assistance. No control employee reported ChatGPT use; self-reported frequency M = 1, SD = 0 on the frequency scale (PDF p. 6, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

participants.exclusions: The initial pool comprised 286 eligible nonmanagerial employees; 36 did not participate because of business travel and illnesses, leaving the final sample of 250 before the subsequent random-assignment step. The procedure then assigns those participants to conditions, supporting n_randomized = 250; no postassignment exclusions are reported. The analyzed sample is 250 employees. Arm-specific randomized and analyzed counts are not printed and remain null (PDF pp. 5-7 and 10, Participants and Procedure, Results, Tables 1 and 3).
participants.who: Nonmanagerial employees in technology, sales/consulting, and administration, excluding employees already experimenting with the ChatGPT API service; 64.8% male, mean age 29.59 years (SD = 4.37). The 250 analyzed employees were nested within 30 supervisors and three departments (PDF pp. 5–6, Participants and Procedure and Results).

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, accessed through the firm's OpenAI API-based interface (model version not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Employees received personal ChatGPT accounts and usage examples for ordinary work; assignment was on August 7, 2023, and the second survey was on August 15, 2023. Self-reported treatment-group usage frequency M = 4.14, SD = 0.81 (1 = never, 5 = very often); usage logs M = 33.72, SD = 8.17. Availability during the privacy-response task is not specified (PDF pp. 5–6, Participants and Procedure; Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

task.description: Ordinary consulting-firm work, with general creative performance rated over the week, plus a written idea-generation task in the second survey: suggestions for protecting employee privacy when companies use digital devices, with responses of at least 70 Chinese characters (PDF p. 6, Dependent Variable: Creativity).
task.duration: Approximately one week of workplace access: assignment August 7, 2023; invitation to the second survey August 15, 2023. No duration for composing the written response is stated (PDF pp. 5–6, Participants and Procedure).

outcomes.name: Creativity (supervisor rating)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Direct supervisors rated employees’ general creative performance over the week using Zhou and George’s (2001) scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree; alpha = .97). Supervisors were approached at the end, were unaware of the experiment, and were blind to hypotheses (PDF p. 6, Dependent Variable: Creativity). This is an employee-level behavior/performance rating, not a rating of an identified output; it is retained as a nonqualifying contextual outcome. Robustness variants include the model with cognitive job resources (Table 3 Model 5: LLM coefficient = 0.71, SE = 0.11, p < .001; PDF p. 10) and models without controls described in the supplement.
outcomes.delay: End-of-intervention rating of general performance over the week; supervisors were approached at the end of the experiment (PDF p. 6).

outcomes.name: Novelty (external raters' rating) of privacy-protection response
outcomes.measure_detail: Two external raters independently rated novelty of each employee’s written privacy-protection response using the consensual assessment technique (1 = least, 5 = most; ICC = .78). Raters were blind to hypotheses and experimental design; neither lay/crowd-worker status nor domain expertise is stated, so measure is null under the codebook's rater-subtype definitions (PDF p. 6, Participants and Procedure; Dependent Variable: Creativity). The analysis is at the employee level. The mediator-adjusted variant has LLM coefficient = 0.13, SE = 0.13 (Table 3 Model 6, PDF p. 10); the 0.17 (SE = 0.08, p = .021) in that model is the cognitive-job-resources coefficient, not the LLM effect (PDF pp. 7 and 10). Models without controls are described in the supplement. Whether ChatGPT was available while composing this response is not stated; availability and question are null rather than assuming either with_ai or after_ai.
outcomes.delay: Response elicited in the second survey, invited August 15, 2023, at the intervention endpoint; no subsequent retention session is reported (PDF p. 6).

Table 3 Model 3, with controls: gamma = 0.25, SE = 0.13, p = .049 (exact p from Results). Analyzed N = 250 employees total; per-arm counts and the t statistic are not printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Table 2; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 3 Model 3; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results; analyzed N in Table 3 note.

outcomes.name: Usefulness (external raters' rating) of privacy-protection response
outcomes.measure_detail: The same two external raters independently rated usefulness of each employee’s written privacy-protection response (consensual assessment technique; 1 = least, 5 = most; ICC = .69; PDF p. 6, Dependent Variable: Creativity). Neither lay/crowd-worker status nor domain expertise is stated, so measure is null under the codebook's rater-subtype definitions. Robustness variants include the model with cognitive job resources (Table 3 Model 7: LLM coefficient = 0.02, SE = 0.12; PDF p. 10) and the model without controls cited in the main Results (PDF p. 6). Whether ChatGPT was available while composing this response is not stated; availability and question are null rather than assuming either with_ai or after_ai.
outcomes.delay: Response elicited in the second survey, invited August 15, 2023, at the intervention endpoint; no subsequent retention session is reported (PDF p. 6).

eligibility.reason: S1 meets all three criteria: employees were individually randomized to ChatGPT assistance versus no LLM assistance in their workplace (PDF pp. 5-6, Participants and Procedure); 250 employees were analyzed (PDF p. 6, Results; PDF pp. 7 and 10, Tables 1 and 3); and external raters scored novelty and usefulness of participants' written privacy-protection responses (PDF p. 6, Dependent Variable: Creativity). Criterion 3 is met by S1-O2 and S1-O3, not by the general supervisor rating. The external raters' qualifications are unspecified, so both measure codes are null; the verified human scoring of output still satisfies criterion 3. Unspecified AI availability during the written task leaves with_ai versus after_ai classification unresolved but does not negate random assignment, the analyzed people count, or output scoring. Question-specific extraction remains pending that clarification.

one_line_finding: Among 250 analyzed employees, ChatGPT access increased supervisor-rated creativity (d = 1.25) and written-response novelty (d = 0.35), while usefulness favored AI in the unadjusted comparison (d = 0.33) but was not significant with controls (p = .136; PDF pp. 6, 8, 10, Results and Tables 2–3).
open_questions: AI availability while composing the privacy-protection response is not stated. Workplace access and use during the week do not establish availability during this survey task; S1-O2 and S1-O3 retain null availability and question. This is also the unresolved reconciliation agreed-field check. It affects with_ai versus after_ai classification, not any of the three eligibility criteria; authors' task instructions or access records would settle it (PDF p. 6, Participants and Procedure and Dependent Variable: Creativity).

The supplied PDF does not report arm-specific randomized or analyzed counts. The total analyzed sample is 250 employees, which already meets criterion 2; no arm split should be derived from the rounded condition mean. Authors' allocation and analysis records would settle the arm counts (PDF pp. 5-7 and 10, Participants and Procedure, Results, Tables 1 and 3).

The supplement is not included and could not be retrieved. The main Results cite Supplemental Table S5 Model 4, whereas footnote 2 cites Supplemental Materials S4 for models without controls; retain both printed references until the supplement resolves their locations and verifies the additional robustness analyses. The main PDF establishes all three eligibility criteria without it (PDF p. 6, Results and footnote 2; PDF p. 7, Exploratory Analyses and Robustness Tests).

The external raters' qualifications and lay/crowd-worker status are not stated. S1-O2 and S1-O3 now have measure = null; human assessment of the written outputs is established and criterion 3 remains met. Authors' rater-recruitment or qualification information would settle the subtype (PDF p. 6, Dependent Variable: Creativity; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure).
notes: All 536 lines of the supplied markdown were read, including the complete reference section and end matter; the saved PDF contains no appended supplement. PDF page numbers include the APA cover page. No effects or sample sizes were computed. Table 2 reports means and SDs but no arm-specific n, and reports p values rather than t statistics; therefore statistics_available omits the complete arm_means_sds_ns bundle and test_statistic while retaining all printed means/SDs in reported. The paper is not preregistered and does not expressly designate outcomes as primary or secondary; primary is not_stated, and is not a selection of the Atlas primary estimate. The supervisor rating remains for completeness but cannot satisfy the output criterion. Null availability/question and external-rater measure values are intentional exceptions to the form's categorical examples, following the instruction not to guess unknown values. The external raters are human assessors, but the document does not establish lay/crowd-worker or expert status. The only confirmed with_ai classification is the weekly supervisor rating, which is not itself scored on output; there is no reported diversity outcome or verified AI-removal assessment. The lead about lower later independent creativity is unsupported: long-term dependence and independent thinking are future-research questions (PDF pp. 11–12, Limitations and Future Directions). Company involvement is corrected to true because the host firm participated; no AI-developer research involvement is stated. Data and materials are available on request but cannot be shared publicly because of a confidentiality agreement; no data/code URL is supplied. Analyses used Stata 16; ethics approval was Renmin University of China protocol #2023R19 (PDF p. 5, Transparency and Openness). Multilevel models nest employees in supervisors and departments (PDF p. 6, Results; PDF p. 10, Table 3). Controls include attitudes/motivation collected in the second, postassignment survey and past performance from company records (PDF p. 6, Procedure and Controls); they should not all be treated as baseline covariates. Self-reported cognitive job resources and metacognitive strategies are not eligible output outcomes. For completeness, the cognitive-job-resources treatment coefficient is gamma = 0.66, SE = 0.10, p < .001 (PDF p. 6, Results; PDF p. 10, Table 3 Model 1). At high metacognitive strategies, reported conditional indirect effects through cognitive job resources are creativity 0.23, 95% CI [0.099, 0.375]; novelty 0.16, 95% CI [0.008, 0.328]; usefulness 0.22, 95% CI [0.083, 0.376] (PDF p. 7, H5 results). These are conditional indirect effects, not separate randomized-arm contrasts. Supplement retrieval via its DOI and the named article DOI was attempted using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; both failed with socket-access error WinError 10013. Reconciliation counts substantive differences and single-form factual/statistical additions, excluding equivalent wording or information merely moved between fields. n_unresolved counts unique substantive issues remaining across discrepancies and agreed-field checks: all A/B differences are resolved, but the shared AI-availability assumption for the written task remains unconfirmed. Final review independently read all 536 markdown lines, including references and end matter, and checked the recorded numerical evidence against PDF pp. 1-2, 5-8, and 10; the supplied 14-page PDF contains no appended supplement or embedded attachment. Both outcome-lens problems were corrected by setting S1-O2.measure and S1-O3.measure to null; assignment and people challenges contained no problems. All four open questions were assessed for eligibility: none changes the three criteria, although written-task AI availability remains necessary for question classification. All entries in reconciliation.differences are resolved; the one unconfirmed agreed-field check is the same written-task AI-availability issue. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as the historical reconciliation, including its superseded human_raters codes; the final object and current outcome fields record the final decisions. During final review, Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296.supp and the named Crossref fallback https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037%2Fapl0001296.supp both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access denied). No supplement statistics were inferred.

open_items.item: AI availability while composing the privacy-protection response (S1-O2/S1-O3, also the unconfirmed reconciliation agreed-field check): authors' task instructions or access records would settle with_ai versus after_ai classification. No eligibility criterion is unresolved.
Arm-specific randomized and analyzed counts: authors' allocation and analysis records would settle them. Total analyzed N = 250 already establishes criterion 2.

Missing supplement and inconsistent no-controls locators (Supplemental Table S5 Model 4 versus Supplemental Materials S4): the supplement would verify the locations and additional robustness statistics. The main PDF establishes all three eligibility criteria.

External-rater qualifications: authors' recruitment or qualification information would distinguish lay/crowd from expert raters. The unknown subtype does not alter criterion 3 because human scoring of written output is verified.
